drivers.driver: The earnings yield of equities is inferior to the risk-free long-term government bond yield [D04].
Extremely high market valuations and lack of bargain opportunities necessitate a disciplined, patient approach [D04, D06].
The requirement to preserve financial strength and insurance-resilience remains paramount over the urge to be fully invested [D05].
Large cash and Treasury-bill holdings provide necessary optionality without the need for immediate deployment into unattractive markets [D01, D06].

final.memo:
We find ourselves in a market where prices are high and the earnings yield on equities fails to provide an attractive premium over the risk-free rate. With the S&P 500 trading at 25.49 times trailing earnings, the margin of safety we demand is absent [D04]. While we prefer owning wonderful businesses, we will not compromise on terms simply to keep our cash moving. 

Our current liquidity position of over $370 billion is not a sign of retreat, but a testament to our discipline [D01, D03]. We continue to evaluate opportunities, but we prioritize the preservation of Berkshire's financial strength and reputation over the institutional imperative to be fully invested [D05, D06]. We remain ready to act decisively when Mr. Market offers us prices that align with our long-term investment criteria.
